title: Cabbage, green, cooked, fat added, NS

content.title: About
content.content: Green cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. capitata) is a leafy vegetable widely used in cooking. When boiled with added fat (oil, butter, or other vegetable fats) it becomes tender and gains a richer flavor. The product is classified as NS (non‑specific) regarding fat type.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cabbage is a rich source of vitamin C, which supports immunity and collagen synthesis.
Glucosinolates in cabbage aid the body’s detoxification processes.
In traditional Russian cuisine cabbage is often boiled with butter or sour cream to enhance taste and absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.
Fresh cabbage can be stored in the refrigerator for up to two weeks in an airtight container.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in cabbage promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: Adding fat enhances the bioavailability of vitamins A, D, E, and K.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A serving of cooked cabbage with a modest amount of fat provides about 70 kcal.

items.title: Sensitivity to glucosinolates
items.content: Large amounts may cause gastrointestinal discomfort in some individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: When salt is added, monitor overall sodium intake.

items.title: Cabbage allergy
items.content: Rare, but possible allergic reactions in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boil cabbage in salted water, then stir in butter or vegetable oil, season with salt and herbs. Serve as a side dish, in soups, or incorporate into casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked cabbage in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags.
